clauses.text:
Executibe Order

EXEMPTION OF GEORGE M. Lewis From CompuLsory RETIREMENT
FoR AGE

WHEREAS, in my judgment, the public interest requires that George M. Lewis,
clerk, Office of the Collector of Taxes, Government of the District of Columbia, who,
during the current month, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic
separation from the service, applicable to him, be exempted from compulsory retire-
ment for age for a period of one year:

NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me
by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S. C., title 5, sec.
715a), I hereby exempt the said George M. Lewis from compulsory retirement for
age for a period of one year ending December 31, 1939.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT
Tue Waite Hovss,
December 2, 1988.

|No. 8019]

U, 8. GOVERNMENT PRINTING OFFICE: 1938

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The only operative command of EO 8019 is its operative paragraph, which exempts George M. Lewis from compulsory retirement for age "for a period of one year ending December 31, 1939". The recital states the President's judgment that the public interest requires exempting George M. Lewis, who, during the current month, "will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service". The command is a time-limited permission for one named employee, so it ended by its own terms on December 31, 1939; that date is recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of that day), and the exclusive reading, under which it ends as that day begins, is the alternative a reviewer should see. No later event is recorded for this clause: no held order text revokes, amends, extends or otherwise cites this order (see the earlier-end check).
